answer.evidence: The assert handling is in radon/visitors.py: ComplexityVisitor.__init__ (line ~157) takes no_assert=False and stores it (line 165). visit_Assert (lines ~257-260) does `self.complexity += not self.no_assert`, which adds 1 only when counting is enabled (bool coerced to int). The flag is propagated to nested visitors at lines ~279 and ~313, so closures and methods behave consistently. The comment at line 235 groups if/with/assert, which is slightly misleading because assert is gated. Review plan: spend most time on radon/raw.py and radon/metrics.py, checking that line counting and aggregate metrics do not depend on or bypass the flag and that no caller reimplements assert scoring. Spend less time on radon/complexity.py, which passes no_assert through, and on radon/visitors.py, where the logic is small and already read. Tests in radon/tests/test_complexity_utils.py cover the default of False. Suggest adding a test that compares the score with no_assert=True and no_assert=False on a snippet containing an assert.
